subject: Throughput guardrails & operational checklist for LumiCloud private GPU pool
messages:
From: Alex Berger <alex.berger@luminacloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumiCloud Infra <infra@luminacloud.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Initial throughput ask for LumiCloud private GPU pool

Hi Irene / Karthik,

Quick context: we’re standing up a private VPC deployment running client inference for our realtime risk product. Ops constraints: on-prem racks (3 racks), 25 Gbps leaf uplinks, and a NATed egress path to our application plane.

We need to validate that the proposed private GPU pool can meet the following operational targets before committing:
- Sustained target: 4,000 tokens/sec aggregate across the pool for baseline model (Llama-70B-qlora-like) under 99th%-latency <= 350ms for tail requests.
- Steady QPS: ~250 concurrent requests (avg prompt ~120 tokens, response ~80 tokens).
- Burst profile: up to 1,000 QPS for bursts lasting up to 10 minutes (spikes due to market events).
- Desired SLA: 99.9% availability during business hours, graceful degradation to smaller model variants on overload.

Primary asks from our side:
1) Sizing guidance (GPU count, expected per-GPU throughput numbers).
2) Network guidance (NIC config, MTU, jumbo frames, RDMA/GPUDirect recommendations).
3) Suggested autoscaling thresholds (queue depth, token backlog, CPU/NIC saturation signals).
4) Runbook for burst handling + KV cache warmup expectations.

We can share topology diagrams and sample traffic traces — attaching a first-pass network diagram. Can we schedule a 30-minute review?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Berger
Director, Infrastructure
LumiCloud

Attachment: network-topology-diagram.png (image/png)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Berger <alex.berger@luminacloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial throughput ask for LumiCloud private GPU pool

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the topology. I pulled together a short checklist and assumptions so we can be concrete in the review. See the attached capacity_assumptions.csv; highlights below.

Summary recommendations (high level):
- Nominal per-GPU sustained tokens/sec we expect for the baseline model (70B, q4_0-like execution): ~450–650 tokens/sec/GPU depending on sequence length and batching. Practical planning should use 500 tokens/sec/GPU as a conservative estimate for sustained steady-state.
- For 4,000 tokens/sec sustained, plan for 8–10 GPUs (conservative 500 tps/GPU -> 8 GPUs; add 2 GPUs for warm-pool headroom and degradation scenarios).
- Burst capacity to support 1,000 QPS (avg 200 tokens total per request) for 10 minutes requires either: short-term burst nodes (2–4 additional GPUs with warmed caches) or a warmed-hot pool + aggressive batching windows (we typically recommend warm-pool approach for predictable bursts).
- Network: 25 Gbps uplinks across three racks should be sufficient if traffic is localized; ensure 2x25G NICs per host or proper bonded links for redundancy. Enable jumbo frames (MTU 9000) and check for NIC offloads. If low-latency RDMA/GPUDirect is available, it materially reduces host CPU overhead for large KV cache movements.
- Autoscaling triggers: token backlog > 5x median for 90s, queue-depth exceeding 300, or sustained GPU util > 72% for 2 minutes. Scale-down policy: below 45% util for 5 minutes with staged cooldowns.
- KV cache warmup: expect 60–180s warmup window depending on model and prefix locality. We recommend pre-warming for scheduled market events.

Next steps I propose:
1) Joint sizing call where we walk through the CSV assumptions and your traffic traces.
2) Lab validation run (PRIVPOOL-4842) where we run a 1-hour sustained load at 1.2x baseline to validate tail latencies.
3) Deliver runbook + canary checklist and a recommended rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).

I attached the CSV and included an internal calc sheet; Karthik will follow with the sizing calculation.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_assumptions.csv (text/csv)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Feb 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial throughput ask for LumiCloud private GPU pool

Irene — I ran a quick back-of-envelope with conservative kernel-level assumptions and attached the detailed math (sizing-math.xlsx). Key notes:
- If we assume 500 tokens/sec/GPU sustained (conservative), 4,000 tokens/sec requires 8 GPUs. With target headroom (30%) for warm-pool and transient spikes, recommend reserving 11 GPUs total.
- For burst handling we model two options:
  a) Warm-hot pool: keep 2 GPUs hot and pre-warmed; bursts absorbed with negligible latency impact but higher idle cost.
  b) Elastic attach: spin up 4 GPUs from a cold pool — mean time to ready for GPU provisioning is ~90–150s (not ideal for 10 minute spikes).
- Network math: 4,000 tokens/sec at ~1.2 KB/token => ~4.8 MB/s aggregate; even with overheads this is < 1 Gbps. The real network pressure is cross-host KV cache sync and bulk model loads during scale events. Recommend cross-host NIC bonding and a dedicated management VLAN for model pulls.
- PCIe/NUMA: validate NUMA alignment for serving docker runtimes; bad pinnings can slash per-GPU throughput by 15–30%.

Action items I need from Dev: lab cluster reservation, confirm GPU image bake time, and a test plan for RDMA toggles.

-Karthik

>   b) Elastic attach: spin up 4 GPUs from a cold pool — mean time to ready for GPU provisioning is ~90–150s (not ideal for 10 minute spikes).
> - Network math: 4,000 tokens/sec at ~1.2 KB/token => ~4.8 MB/s aggregate; even with overheads this is < 1 Gbps. The real network pressure is cross-host KV cache sync and bulk model loads during scale events.

Thanks — I can allocate a 12-GPU lab cluster and run the PRIVPOOL-4842 job next week. I’ll toggle RDMA on/off and capture GPU util, p95/p99 latencies, queue depth, and NIC counters.

Planned validation steps (lab run):
1) Baseline sustained run at 1.0x (60 minutes) to measure sustained throughput and p99 latency.
2) Ramp to 1.2x sustained for 30 minutes to observe degradation modes.
3) 10-minute bursts generated to observe warm-pool vs cold-provision behavior.
4) Network experiments: jumbo frames on/off, NIC offload toggles, and RDMA flow.

I’ll post results to the Drive folder and flag any infra blockers.

— Dev
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 25 Feb 2028 10:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial throughput ask for LumiCloud private GPU pool

Alex — thanks for the prompt. We have a plan and a lab validation slot next week. Quick bullets and next steps: 

- Sizing recommendation: target 11 GPUs (8 for steady-state + 3 for warm/prefetch/burst headroom).
- Autoscale & SLOs: triggers and scale policies as in the CSV; fallback model variant defined in runbook.
- Network: enable jumbo frames, bond NICs for management/model-pull traffic, and prefer GPUDirect/RDMA if available; ensure model pulls happen off a dedicated management VLAN to avoid application plane interference.
- Runbook & canary: deliverable after lab run; will include canary checklist, rollback triggers, and a scheduled 30-min kickoff.

Scheduling: I booked a 30-min joint review on your Calendly link for Tue 2028-02-29 09:00 PT (confirm if that works). Lab job: PRIVPOOL-4842 scheduled Wed 2028-03-06.

Attachments: runbook-private-pool.md (markdown) — draft will be updated post-lab. Drive folder with all artifacts: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1qWz-priv-pool-review

We’ll follow up with the lab results and then finalize the mutual action plan and rollout cadence.

Best,
Irene
